summary: Defines a human-readable string format for LDAP search filters, which LDAP otherwise sends as network encodings, so applications can write filters in a common textual form. It was replaced by RFC 1960.

eli5.summary: A search request can be written as plain text, like a sentence you can read. This memo sets one common way to write it.

questions: how to write an ldap filter
how do you write an ldap filter
subtitle: Writing LDAP search requests in plain text instead of network encoding

tldr.problem: LDAP search filters are normally sent in ASN.1 network encoding, which is not human-readable. Applications and system administrators need a common, readable text format for writing filters.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1558 defines a string syntax using prefix notation with parentheses and operators: & for AND, | for OR, ! for NOT, and comparison operators like = (equal), >= (greater or equal), ~= (approximately equal), and =* (present).
tldr.outcome: This became a standard way to express LDAP filters in configuration files and command-line tools. RFC 1960 later standardized this more formally.

today: RFC 1558 is Informational. RFC 1960 later standardized LDAP filter syntax more formally as a Standards Track specification. The filter format defined here has become the standard way to write LDAP queries in tools and configuration files.

sections.title: Filters in Plain Text
sections.content: The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) defines a network representation of search filters that is encoded using ASN.1 Basic Encoding Rules. This binary format is efficient for transmission but not human-readable. RFC 1558 defines a text string format that applications can use to write LDAP search filters in a common, readable way. The format is called prefix notation because operators and test types come before their operands.
sections.eli5: LDAP searches are sent in a complicated computer code over the network. This document shows how to write them as plain text that people can read and understand.

sections.title: The Filter String Format
sections.content: A filter is enclosed in parentheses and consists of one or more comparisons or logical combinations. The logical operators are: & for AND (all conditions must match), | for OR (at least one must match), and ! for NOT (the condition must not match). A simple comparison uses the form attribute operator value, where the operator is = (equal), >= (greater or equal), <= (less or equal), or ~= (approximately equal). The =* operator tests whether an attribute is present. Substring matching uses wildcards where an asterisk character stands for any sequence of characters. Special characters (asterisk, parentheses, and backslash) must be escaped with a backslash.
sections.eli5: Write conditions inside parentheses. Use ampersand for AND, pipe for OR, and exclamation for NOT. Write attribute equals value to test if something matches. Use the asterisk symbol as a wildcard for parts of words.

sections.title: Examples of Filters
sections.content: (cn=Babs Jensen) finds entries where the common name is exactly Babs Jensen. (!(cn=Tim Howes)) finds all entries except those with common name Tim Howes. (&(objectClass=Person)(|(sn=Jensen)(cn=Babs J*))) combines: AND this entry is of class Person AND it has surname Jensen OR it has a common name starting with Babs J. (o=univ*of*mich*) matches organization names containing univ...of...mich in that order, such as University of Michigan.
sections.eli5: These are real examples: 'find Babs Jensen', 'find anyone NOT named Tim Howes', 'find people whose last name is Jensen OR whose first name starts with Babs', and 'find universities with Michigan in the name'.

data.title: LDAP Filter Examples
data.code:
(cn=John Smith)          Simple equality
(!(cn=Admin))             Negation (NOT)
(&(cn=John)(o=Acme))      Conjunction (AND)
(|(cn=John)(cn=Jane))     Disjunction (OR)
(cn=John*)                Wildcard (starts with)
(cn=*Smith)               Wildcard (ends with)
(cn=*ohn*)                Wildcard (contains)
(cn=*)
                          Presence test (has attribute)
